en: Saṃyutta Nikāya 26.1 (SN 26.1, PTS SN iii 228) 1. Uppādavagga Cakkhusutta (The Discourse on the Eye) “Bhikkhus, the eye arises; having arisen, it passes away. Its arising is suffering, its passing away is suffering. The ear arises; having arisen, it passes away. Its arising is suffering, its passing away is suffering. The nose arises; having arisen, it passes away. Its arising is suffering, its passing away is suffering. The tongue arises; having arisen, it passes away. Its arising is suffering, its passing away is suffering. The body arises; having arisen, it passes away. Its arising is suffering, its passing away is suffering. The mind arises; having arisen, it passes away. Its arising is suffering, its passing away is suffering.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.

"Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence, the manifestation, and the appearance of the eye—that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.
Whatever is the arising, the persistence... of the ear... [and so on for the other sense bases].
Whatever is the arising and persistence of the nose...
whatever is the arising and persistence of the tongue...
whatever is the arising and persistence of the body...
Whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of the mind, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.
And whatever, monks, is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of the eye, that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, and the passing away of aging and death.
Whatever is the cessation of the ear... [and so on].
Whatever is the cessation of the nose … whatever is the cessation of the tongue … whatever is the cessation of the body …
“The cessation, the subsiding, the passing away of the mind: this is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, the passing away of aging and death.
Thus it was said. First. *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 26.2.
1. The Chapter on Arising.
The Discourse on Form.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
“Monks, whatever is the arising, the persistence, the manifestation, and the appearance of forms— that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the appearance of aging and death.
Whatever is [the arising] of sounds… whatever is [the arising] of odors…”

Whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of tastes... whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of tangibles... whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of mental phenomena—this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.
But, monks, that which is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of forms—that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, and the passing away of aging and death.
That which is [the cessation] of sounds... that which is [the cessation] of odors... [and so forth].
That which is the cessation, the subsiding, the passing away of tastes... of tangibles...
of mental phenomena: this is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, the passing away of aging and death.”
The Second.
Saṃyutta Nikāya 26.3 (SN 26.3, PTS SN iii 229) 1.
The Chapter on Arising (Uppādavagga)
The Discourse on Consciousness. Setting: Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence, ... [and so forth] ... of eye-consciousness...”
The manifestation of aging and death …pe… whatever is the arising and persistence of mind-consciousness …pe… the manifestation of aging and death.
But, monks, that which is the cessation of eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the passing away of aging-and-death … [and so on] … that which is the cessation of mind-consciousness … [and so on] …
“The cessation of aging and death.
Third.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 26.4 (SN 26.4, PTS SN iii 229).
1. The Chapter on Arising:
Discourse on Contact.
Setting at Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence … [and so on] … the manifestation of eye-contact … [and so on] … the arising,
the persistence … [and so on] … of mind-contact …”
The manifestation of aging and death.
But, monks, the cessation of eye-contact …pe… the passing away of aging and death …pe…
“The cessation of mind-contact … [and so on] … the subsiding of aging and death.
The fourth.

Saṁyutta Nikāya 26.5 Uppādavagga Samphassajasutta “Bhikkhus, whatever is felt born of eye-contact is included within suffering; it is not included within happiness. Whatever is felt born of ear-contact... born of nose-contact... born of tongue-contact... born of body-contact... born of mind-contact is included within suffering; it is not included within happiness.”
At Sāvatthī.
"Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence... [and so on] ...the manifestation of aging-and-death regarding feeling born of eye-contact...
[and so on] ...whatever is the arising, the persistence... [and so on] ...regarding feeling born of mind-contact."
The manifestation of aging and death.
But, monks, the cessation, the subsiding of feeling born of eye-contact … [and so on] … the passing away of aging and death … [and so on].
“The cessation, the subsiding, the passing away of feeling born of mind-contact: this is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, the passing away of aging and death.
Thus it was said.
The fifth. *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 26.6 (SN 26.6, PTS SN iii 230).
1. The Chapter on Arising.
Discourse on Perception.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of perception of forms...

[and so on] ...whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of perception of phenomena— this is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.”
"But, monks, as for the cessation of perception of forms...
[and so on] ...the subsiding of aging and death...
[and so on] ...the cessation, the pacification, the disappearance of perception of phenomena—this is the cessation of suffering, the pacification of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death."
Sixth. Saṁyutta Nikāya 26.7 (SN 26.7, PTS SN iii 230) 1.
Uppādavagga (The Chapter on Arising)
The Discourse on Volitional Intent.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, whatever arising there is of volitional intent regarding form, whatever persistence... [and so forth].”
The manifestation of aging and death...

[and so on] ...whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of volition regarding phenomena (*dhamma-saṃcetanā*), that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.
And whatever, monks, is the cessation of volition regarding forms (*rūpa-saṃcetanā*)... [and so on].
“The cessation of aging and death...
that which is the cessation, the subsiding, the disappearance of volition regarding phenomena—this is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, the disappearance of aging and death.
The seventh.

Saṃyutta Nikāya 26.8 (SN 26.8, PTS SN iii 230) 1. Uppādavagga Taṇhāsutta (The Discourse on Craving) “Bhikkhus, craving arises in dependence on feeling; feeling arises in dependence on contact; contact arises in dependence on the six sense bases; the six sense bases arise in dependence on name-and-form; name-and-form arises in dependence on consciousness; consciousness arises in dependence on formations; and formations arise in dependence on ignorance. “Bhikkhus, when ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises, formations cease; with the cessation of formations, consciousness ceases; with the cessation of consciousness, name-and-form ceases; with the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense bases cease; with the cessation of the six sense bases, contact ceases; with the cessation of contact, feeling ceases; with the cessation of feeling, craving ceases.”
At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence, [the growth, the increase, and the maturation] of craving for forms...
[and so on] ...is the manifestation of aging and death... [and so on] ...”
Whatever arising, persistence, production, and manifestation there is of craving for phenomena—that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.
But, monks, whatever cessation of craving for forms...
[and so on] ...the passing away of aging and death... [and so on].
“The cessation, the subsiding, the passing away of craving for existence—that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, the passing away of aging and death.
The eighth.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 26.9 (SN 26.9, PTS SN iii 231).
1. The Chapter on Arising.
Discourse on the Elements.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
“Monks, whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of the earth element … [and so on] … the manifestation of aging and death; whatever is the [arising,
persistence, production, and manifestation] of the water element … the fire element …”

Whatever arising, persistence, generation, and manifestation there is of the air element … of the space element … of the consciousness element, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.
But, monks, that which is the cessation of the earth element … [and so on] … the passing away of aging and death;
that which is the cessation of the water element … that which is the cessation of the fire element … [and so on] … the passing away of aging and death.
Whatever is the cessation of the air element,
whatever is the cessation of the space element,
whatever is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of the consciousness element— this is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, and the passing away of aging and death.”
The Ninth.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 26.10 (SN 26.10, PTS SN iii 231) 1.
The Chapter on Arising (Uppādavagga)
The Discourse on the Aggregates. At Sāvatthī.

"Bhikkhus, whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of form—that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death."
Who [clings] to feeling … who [clings] to perception … who [clings] to volitional formations …

Whatever is the arising, the persistence, the production, and the manifestation of consciousness, that is the arising of suffering, the persistence of diseases, and the manifestation of aging and death.

But, monks, whatever is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of form, that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, and the passing away of aging and death. Whatever [is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away] of feeling...

That which is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of perception... that which is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of volitional formations... that which is the cessation, the subsiding, and the passing away of consciousness—this is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of diseases, and the passing away of aging and death.”
Tenth. The First Chapter on Arising.
Its summary verse:
The eye and forms, consciousness,
contact and feeling,
perception, volition, and craving.
"Those ten by way of element and aggregate.
The Connected Discourse on Arising is finished.
